items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: But we have people in there like Bob Cranshaw and Jimmy Owens and people that are really and --

ctx.x: There’s a reason you’re doing that. That’s a good one. How’s the musician’s union been for you over the years?

It’s been kind of dormant really. But we have people in there like Bob Cranshaw and Jimmy Owens and people that are really and -- And at one time Benny Powell was in there really pushing them really to help, to bring jazz musicians up to par. So it looks, because I did a lot of things, I was in the Playboy Club for instance once for a while, playing with Kai Winding, then I had my own quartet there or a while. Because I just wanted to stay around town. It was a good place, to have a nice, steady jazz gig and you…
Yeah. It’s unfortunate that so many musicians don’t end up with what they should. Does the music tend to keep you young do you think?

items.title: Jimmy Owens — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Earl May played bass, but then Earl May left and I told Herbie Mann... So, it was a good band, you know?

ctx.x: Now where were we with Mingus? How long were you with Mingus?

I was actually with Mingus two times. I worked with Mingus in 1964 at Birdland. That was the band that was playing the music of black saint and the cinder lady. That was Rolf Ericson, Lonnie Hillyer and myself in the trumpet section. Britt Woodman played trombone and then Carlie Mariano played alto saxophone, Pepper Adams played baritone, and Eric Dolphy would come in and sit in sometimes. We worked at Birdland for two weeks, and Birdland being the original Birdland at 52nd street and Broadway. The first week we…

not talk over it, and people had to listen. It was very interesting. The control that John Coltrane had over everyone in his group, you know? Elvin Jones just could not get faster because Coltrane just kept playing that same tempo instead of getting faster, he would hold everyone back. It was very interesting. So, that was the time with Mingus, we played some other festivals. I think we played in Boston or something.
